Introduction

The electric vehicle revolution is no longer a future possibility: it's happening now, and Los Angeles is at the forefront of this transformation. As more businesses and homeowners across California switch to electric vehicles, the demand for reliable charging infrastructure has become critical. At Shaffer Construction, Inc., we understand that investing in EV charging infrastructure isn't just an environmental statement; it's an essential investment in the future of sustainable transportation. Whether you're a property owner in Los Angeles looking to install residential EV chargers or a business considering commercial charging solutions, understanding the importance and current landscape of EV charging infrastructure is the first step toward making an informed decision.

The Explosive Growth of EV Charging Infrastructure in 2025

The scale of infrastructure expansion happening in 2025 is remarkable. According to the International Energy Agency's Global EV Outlook 2025, the United States now has approximately 196,000 public charging ports, a nearly 6-fold increase from just 30,000 in 2016. Forecasts indicate that 16,700 new ports will open in 2025 alone, demonstrating unprecedented momentum. In California, the numbers are even more impressive: the state has exceeded 201,000 publicly available EV charging ports, surpassing the total number of gasoline nozzles statewide. Shaffer Construction stays ahead of these trends to ensure our Los Angeles clients have access to the latest charging technology and installation methods.

For property owners and businesses in Los Angeles specifically, this growth represents a unique opportunity. With 94% of Californians now living within just 10 minutes of an EV charger, the infrastructure is becoming increasingly accessible. However, this rapid expansion also means that proper planning and professional installation are more important than ever. Our team at Shaffer Construction helps Los Angeles property owners navigate the complexities of charger selection, electrical upgrades, and permitting to ensure successful installations.

Los Angeles: Leading the Nation in EV Charging Infrastructure Investment

Los Angeles has emerged as the undisputed leader in EV charging infrastructure across the United States. The city now boasts 36,000 public chargers serving its 3 million residents, representing a remarkable 77% increase in available charging infrastructure over just the past two years. This aggressive expansion reflects the city's commitment to sustainability and the growing demands of its EV-driving population. In November 2025, the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation announced an ambitious project to install 90 new Level 2 curbside chargers throughout the city, further strengthening the charging network and ensuring equitable access across all neighborhoods.

Los Angeles County has also received significant federal funding to advance its infrastructure goals. The county, city, and Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority combined received $15 million in grants to construct over 1,250 EV charging stations, with a particular focus on underserved communities. Additionally, the California Energy Commission launched a $55 million project in 2025 dedicated to installing high-powered electric vehicle charging stations throughout the state. These investments demonstrate that Los Angeles and California are serious about supporting the EV transition, and businesses and homeowners should consider this momentum when planning their own charging infrastructure projects. Shaffer Construction has partnered with many Los Angeles property owners to take advantage of available incentives and funding opportunities for their installations.

Environmental and Economic Benefits of EV Charging Infrastructure Investment

Investing in EV charging infrastructure delivers substantial environmental benefits that extend far beyond individual vehicles. According to research on sustainable transportation and energy solutions, electric vehicles convert 60 to 70 percent of grid electricity into actual movement, compared to only 20 to 30 percent efficiency for traditional gasoline and diesel engines. This dramatic difference means that widespread EV adoption could reduce global CO2 emissions by approximately 1.5 billion metric tons annually. For Los Angeles, a city historically challenged by air quality issues, this transition is particularly important and impactful. Shaffer Construction is proud to contribute to this environmental transformation by helping property owners install the infrastructure necessary to support cleaner transportation options.

The economic benefits are equally compelling. Property owners and businesses that install EV charging infrastructure often find that it attracts customers, increases property values, and generates additional revenue streams. For commercial properties in Los Angeles, EV chargers have become an expected amenity that enhances customer satisfaction and aligns with corporate sustainability goals. Homeowners who install residential chargers can take advantage of federal tax credits covering up to 30% of hardware and installation costs, with a maximum credit of $1,000. As discussed in our comprehensive guide on EV charging infrastructure for Los Angeles property owners, there are numerous financial incentives available to offset installation costs. Shaffer Construction helps our clients in Los Angeles identify and access these benefits to maximize their investment returns.

Understanding Residential and Commercial EV Charger Installation Requirements

Installing EV charging infrastructure requires careful planning and adherence to electrical codes, particularly the National Electrical Code Article 625, which governs Electric Vehicle Charging Systems. For residential installations, most Los Angeles homeowners opt for Level 2 chargers operating at 240 volts, which provide convenient overnight charging. A typical residential Level 2 charger installation costs between $800 and $2,500, depending on existing electrical infrastructure and the complexity of the installation. More complex installations requiring significant electrical panel upgrades can cost up to $4,000. The good news is that federal tax credits and some California state incentives can substantially reduce these out-of-pocket expenses.

Commercial installations are more complex and typically more expensive, but they offer significant benefits for Los Angeles businesses. Level 2 commercial chargers range from $3,000 to $12,000 per charger, depending on site conditions and electrical infrastructure. DC fast chargers, which are increasingly popular at high-traffic commercial locations, cost significantly more: typically between $80,000 and $250,000 per charger. However, the investment pays dividends through increased customer traffic, enhanced brand reputation, and alignment with Los Angeles's sustainability initiatives. Our team at Shaffer Construction specializes in evaluating your specific property requirements, assessing electrical capacity, designing systems that meet code compliance, and managing all aspects of the installation process. We have extensive experience with both residential and commercial projects across Los Angeles, ensuring installations meet or exceed all safety and performance standards.

Planning, Funding, and Implementing Your EV Charging Project

Successful EV charging infrastructure projects require strategic planning and professional expertise. As described in more detail in our article about planning EV charger infrastructure in Los Angeles, property owners need to carefully consider their charging needs, electrical capacity, available funding, and timeline. For those considering a project, the first step is assessing your property's electrical infrastructure. Many Los Angeles properties may require electrical panel upgrades, trenching, or conduit installation to support chargers, work that should only be performed by licensed electrical contractors like Shaffer Construction.

Federal and state funding programs have made 2025 an ideal time to invest in charging infrastructure. The Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit provides tax incentives, while the Federal Highway Administration's NEVI Formula Program offers to cover up to 80% of certain project costs. California's $55 million high-powered charging initiative and the county's $15 million investment in underserved communities represent unprecedented opportunities for Los Angeles property owners. Whether you're looking at residential EV charger installation or commercial EV charging solutions, Shaffer Construction can guide you through the entire process, from initial site assessment through final installation and inspection.

The Future of EV Charging Infrastructure and Your Role in It

Looking ahead, the future of EV charging infrastructure is both exciting and critical. The U.S. Department of Energy estimates that to support 33 million electric vehicles projected to be on the road by 2030, approximately 1 million additional public chargers will be needed, with roughly 170,000 being DC fast chargers. This projection underscores the ongoing importance of both public infrastructure investment and private property owner participation. Los Angeles property owners who install chargers now position themselves as leaders in the sustainability movement while also benefiting from incentives and competitive advantages before they disappear. The window of opportunity for maximum federal and state support is open now, investments made in 2025 may qualify for benefits that won't be available in future years.

At Shaffer Construction, we're committed to helping Los Angeles property owners and businesses navigate the complexities of EV charging infrastructure. Whether you need a single residential charger or a comprehensive commercial charging network, our team combines technical expertise, regulatory knowledge, and project management excellence to deliver installations that exceed expectations and serve your property for years to come.

Conclusion

Investing in EV charging infrastructure is one of the most important decisions Los Angeles property owners can make for the environment, their communities, and their own long-term interests. The growth of EV adoption, combined with unprecedented federal and state funding, makes 2025 the ideal time to install charging infrastructure. From the environmental benefits of reduced carbon emissions to the economic advantages of increased property values and customer attraction, the case for EV charging investment is compelling and multifaceted.
